name: heart
note: Assembles the AQA GCSE heart from BodyParts3D elemental meshes.

Part names are the structure names exactly as heart.json labels them, because the isolate tool shows a part's name to the class verbatim (`Isolated: Right atrium`) and the renderer contract forbids inventing one. They bind to hotspot ids by slug: slugify(part name) == the id after the specimen prefix.

`parts` is a PARTITION — each elemental file is assigned to the single most specific structure that claims it, so no triangle appears twice and the watertight gate stays meaningful. BodyParts3D does not decompose the heart into one mesh per named structure: its elemental meshes are claimed by several named concepts at once (the tricuspid leaflets are simultaneously part of the right atrium and the right ventricle).
TWO TREES, AND WHY (MRB-222).

BodyParts3D ships its release twice, built up two different ways: a partof tree and an isa tree. Until MRB-222 this recipe used only the partof one, and could not show the single fact the heart is taught for — that the left ventricle wall is thicker than the right.

The partof tree's `wall of left ventricle` (FMA9556) and `wall of right ventricle` (FMA9533) are not walls. They are papillary-muscle lumps, covering 2.5% and 10% of the directions around their own cavities. A name is not geometry.

The isa tree carries `wall of ventricle` (FMA13884) as a SINGLE element, FJ2428, which is absent from the partof archive entirely. It encloses both ventricular lumens at 91.3% angular coverage and measures, across 13 short-axis levels, an LV free wall of 9.39mm against an RV free wall of 3.53mm — a ratio of 2.66:1. Textbook is 8-12mm, 3-5mm, about 3:1. That element is this specimen's `Ventricular myocardium`.
THE TWO TREES SHARE A COORDINATE FRAME — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED.

All 1,258 elements present in both archives are byte-identical below their header comments; the only difference in any of them is the `Representation ID` and `Build-up logic` lines. So a part drawn from the isa tree drops into an assembly of partof parts with no transform reconciliation, and the myocardium lands around the cavity casts rather than beside them.
THE FOUR CHAMBERS ARE NOW THE CAVITY CASTS ALONE.

The papillary lumps (FJ2418, FJ2419, FJ2429, FJ2430, FJ2432, FJ2437) have left the assembly. They sit inside FJ2428's volume, so keeping them would double-count triangles and break the watertight gate. That also makes the chambers' `blood-*` appearance tokens literally true rather than a convenient reading: the geometry IS the blood, and the muscle is a separate part beside it.
PREPARATION OF FJ2428 — one documented command, not a hand edit.

FJ2428 ships 7 zero-volume sliver components holding all of its topology errors (b0/o7/m14). Dropping them costs 1.853 of 160,720 cubic mm, 0.0012% of the volume, and makes it watertight. `--min-volume 1` does NOT separate them; 100 does. Produce the file this recipe names with:
python3 tools/inspect_source_mesh.py clean <isa-obj-dir> FJ2428 <isa-obj-dir>/FJ2428.clean100.obj --min-volume 100
It deletes components; it never adds, moves or thickens geometry. Result: 35,232 triangles, watertight YES, sha256 74350051e81da31a2f0ca025a2957ef697618ac2b8850599eddcd5eb3da32f8a.
THE TRIANGLE BUDGET.

The raw assembly is 142,736 triangles against a 60,000 gate, so the pipeline's simplifier does the same work it has always done here — the shipping heart before MRB-222 was 111,518 raw triangles reduced to 54,990. What is NEW is that `Ventricular myocardium` is marked `preserve` and is never simplified. Its median edge is 1.62mm against a 3.53mm right-ventricular free wall, about two triangles across, so uniform decimation eats the RIGHT ventricle first and destroys the measurement while leaving something that still looks like a heart. Everything else pays for that protection out of the remaining budget.

Two of heart.json's fourteen hotspots still have no part here and are anchored by coordinate alone: the septum (BodyParts3D names no separately addressable septum; it is interventricular myocardium, now inside FJ2428 rather than absent) and the sino-atrial node (no conducting tissue is modelled anywhere in the dataset).
Run: python3 tools/prepare_specimen.py tools/recipes/heart.recipe.json \
--obj-dir partof=<extracted partof_BP3D_4.0_obj_99> \
--obj-dir isa=<extracted isa_BP3D_4.0_obj_99>

source.release: BP3D 4.0, partof AND isa trees, 99% reduction

transform.note: BodyParts3D is +x anatomical left, +y posterior, +z superior, in millimetres within a whole-body frame (the heart sits around z=1230). Converted to glTF's y-up and recentred on its own bounds so authored position3d values are small numbers about the origin.

parts.name: Right atrium
sources: FMA7096 right atrium — the cavity cast alone

parts.name: Right ventricle
sources: FMA7098 right ventricle — the cavity cast alone
excluded: FJ2419, FJ2430, FJ2437 — papillary muscle and the partof tree's misnamed `wall of right ventricle`, which covers only 10% of the directions around this cavity. All three lie inside FJ2428's volume and are carried by `Ventricular myocardium` instead.

parts.name: Left atrium
sources: FMA7097 left atrium — the cavity cast alone

parts.name: Left ventricle
sources: FMA7101 left ventricle — the cavity cast alone
excluded: FJ2418, FJ2429 — papillary muscle and the partof tree's misnamed `wall of left ventricle`, which covers only 2.5% of the directions around this cavity. Both lie inside FJ2428's volume and are carried by `Ventricular myocardium` instead.

parts.name: Ventricular myocardium
sources: FMA13884 wall of ventricle, isa tree, sliver components removed
parts.note: No hotspot: heart.json names no `Ventricular myocardium`, and inventing one would be authoring anatomy outside the science gate. It therefore takes the specimen-level appearance and cutMaterial defaults, which is why heart.json sets them. `preserve` is load-bearing — see the triangle-budget note above.

parts.name: Right atrial wall
parts.note: No hotspot, by the same reasoning as the myocardium. Split out of `Right atrium` in MRB-222 so that every chamber part is a cavity cast and every wall part is muscle, rather than the two being mixed inside one node.

parts.name: Tricuspid valve
sources: FMA7234 tricuspid valve (anterior, posterior, septal leaflets)

parts.name: Vena cava
sources: FMA10951 inferior vena cava, thoracic course only
excluded: FJ3659 — the abdominal course of the inferior vena cava, spanning z 951-1095mm while the heart itself sits at 1180-1260mm. Excluded on the same principle already applied to the aorta (ascending and arch kept, descending and abdominal dropped) and to the pulmonary vessels (extrapulmonary part kept, intrapulmonary dropped): the specimen carries the cardiac segment of each great vessel, not its distal course. BodyParts3D names no subdivision of the inferior vena cava, so this is excluded by element file rather than by concept. Costs 1,670 triangles and takes the bounding radius from 206mm to 146mm, so the heart renders 30% larger in the same frame.
